title: Useful Markings--But Uneven Stamping Spoils Cutting Board's Looks
text:
Useful Markings--But Uneven Stamping Spoils Cutting Board's Looks. Because I have a small kitchen with limited countertop work space, and cook for only two people, I prefer small cutting boards like this FRED CHEESE DEGREES BAMBOO CUTTING BOARD. The markings on it are actually quite helpful for when I want to cut things (not just cheese) into uniform wedges, cubes, or chunks.

However, I doubt that the markings will remain visible for long. The markings are cut or burned quite shallowly into the bamboo board, as if incised by a hot metal stamping device (akin to a child's woodburner). Also, the markings on my board are not as consistently precise as those on the board in the product page photo.

I will try to preserve the markings for as long as possible by always using the plain, unmarked side of the cutting board when I don't need the markings. This cutting board is NOT dishwasher safe--it's hand washable only, not to be left submerged in water, and should be oiled regularly to prevent drying out.

My small (6" x 8"), plain, dishwasher-safe Epicurean cutting board (about $11 on Amazon), will definitely remain my favorite, but this larger (7" x 8"), fancier, pricier (about $25 on Amazon) cutting board is useful, too. If the markings were stamped precisely, I would love it, and would recommend it as a gift for almost any cook. Unfortunately, the markings are NOT precise, so it's not very good looking. I rate it at 3 stars ("It's okay" on the official Amazon scale).
